findings.detail: scored 0 — The answer correctly states the subsample qualifier rule for turbidity temperature DO and Eh but it refuses the flow-cell sampling question the rubric expected a real answer for and omits the storage limits and the on-site/in-situ turbidity guidance. Unmet: States plainly that a discrete turbidity sample must not be collected from the discharge passing through the flow-through chamber holding the other sensors; Gives the storage limits if the sample cannot be read on site: clean amber bottle out of sunlight chilled at or below 4 C held no longer than 24 hours; Notes turbidity is time sensitive and should be measured on site preferably in situ

scored 0 — The answer misses all four must-contain points and instead resolves the imagined conflict by telling the user to use the A6.8 numbers a must-not violation. Unmet: States plainly that the two tables give the same stabilisation criteria and do not conflict; States the general field-measurement chapter itself points multiparameter users to the multiparameter chapter for criteria of the same kind; States the criteria are standard sensor stabilisation criteria and that actual sensor accuracy varies by model and manufacturer a separate matter; For persistent variability extends equilibration and records additional measurements then reports the median of the final five or more readings or selects a representative final reading using site knowledge and professional judgment documenting the decision

scored 0 — The answer declines the A6.8 criteria entirely so none of the must-contain points about the example form's ±0.1 and ±0.3 pH-unit criteria or the comparison are made even though it correctly states A6.4's 0.05 pH-unit final-buffer check. Unmet: Attributes ±0.1 pH unit to the A6.8 example field form's calibration criterion; Attributes ±0.3 pH unit below 75 µS/cm to that example form; Distinguishes the form's conductivity-dependent criteria from A6.4's final-buffer check requiring agreement within 0.05 pH unit of the certified value at calibration temperature

scored 0 — The answer is a refusal that withholds the requested table values and comparison making none of the must-contain points though it avoids the must-not violations. Unmet: gives the USGS table value at 20.0 C and 760 mmHg as about 9.09 mg/L; gives the EPA chart value at 20 C and 760 mmHg as about 9.06 mg/L; States the difference is 0.03 mg/L and assesses its significance against the applicable procedure; notes the USGS values are generated from the Benson and Krause equations; Compares the 0.03 mg/L difference with the USGS saturation-check tolerance of ±0.2 mg/L; advises using the table belonging to whichever protocol the work is being done under consistently

scored 0 — The answer makes several must-contain points but violates a must-not by asserting the EPA SOP and USGS manual 'differ' without support and it omits the each-sampling-location exemption the qualification of pre-check data the measurement-mode post-check procedure and the QA-plan condition. Unmet: End-of-day calibration check except when calibrated at each sampling location under the stated exemption; Midday drift: recalibrate before treating later data as unaffected; preceding data qualified; DO post-calibration check done in measurement mode recording DO temperature and barometric pressure against an oxygen-solubility chart; SOP's own drift criteria apply only when the project QA plan does not specify its own

scored 0 — The answer gives the multiplication method and cites the salinity-correction table but withholds the requested factor for 20.0 °C at 50 000 µS/cm refusing it as not in the excerpts which is a refusal of a figure a must-contain point asks for. Unmet: Gives 0.8235 as the factor for 20.0 °C at 50 000 µS/cm

scored 0 — The answer checks expiry and storage but never mentions flocculation and it advises resuspending and using the settled bottle without any flocculation check violating a must-not item. Unmet: States calibrants with flocculated suspensions must not be used; Requires checking whether the settled layer is reversible settling or flocculation plus labeled expiry and storage compliance and rejects flocculated/expired/compromised calibrant

scored 0 — The answer tells the operator the order is arbitrary for the other three sensors ("you can start with any of them") and misses every ordering point — temperature first conductance before pH DO/ORP after pH and the ionic-strength carryover rationale — so a must-not item is violated. Unmet: States order matters and gives a recommended sequence; Places temperature first in the sequence; Places specific conductance before pH; Places dissolved oxygen and then ORP after pH; Explains sequence runs from lower to higher ionic strength to avoid carryover bias; Notes pH buffers and electrode filling solutions are high ionic strength and would contaminate conductivity calibration

scored 0 — The answer is a bare refusal that withholds the requested content and makes none of the rubric's must-contain points though it violates no must-not item. Unmet: Corpus gives no rule for deciding which part of a long record may be kept; No source gives an allowable drift rate (per-day/per-week); No procedure for correcting/adjusting a record after recovery; Turbidity chapter's fouling check (calibrant before/after cleaning percent difference); Fouling check quantifies one sensor's condition not an acceptance rule; EPA SOP: calibrate before deployment check on recovery defer drift criteria to QA plan default post-calibration criteria; Declines to convert EPA post-calibration criteria into a keep-or-discard threshold; EPA default criteria are a pass/fail check at recovery failing data qualified not discarded
